title: Costs, slippage and fill assumptions
objectives: Apply separate adverse half-spread, slippage and per-unit fee assumptions to signed fills and reconcile a fixed-path gross/net round trip.
Stress capacity, affordability and no-fill scenarios without inferring executable size/queue priority from OHLC touches or treating scenario costs as calibrated market truth.
Apply costs, slippage and fill assumptions invariants safely and identify scope boundaries.
motivation: Execution cost has several reference points. A quoted bid/ask spread, arrival-midpoint shortfall, decision-to-arrival move, market impact, fees and financing are not interchangeable.

blocks.md: Execution cost has several reference points. A quoted bid/ask spread, arrival-midpoint shortfall, decision-to-arrival move, market impact, fees and financing are not interchangeable. Avoid double counting: if the fill price is already the ask for a buy, do not add another half-spread just because a cost field exists. Slippage relative to an expected price can be favorable or adverse in real trading. Our scenario uses ONLY nonnegative adverse add-ons to an explicitly synthetic opening reference, not a statistical slippage estimate or necessarily a traded bar open.

The complete source repeats the prior engine. Buy execution=opening_reference+half_spread+adverse_slip; sell=reference-half_spread-adverse_slip. A fee_per_unit is charged on either filled side. All are integer cents per share, not basis points or percent. Costs are zero for zero fills. All opening references must exceed the sum of costs in this bounded sell-proceeds contract. This is an own symmetric stress scenario, not the broker/venue's actual fee table and not market impact calibrated to size.

blocks.title: Separate price drag from commission
items: Same 2-share buy 110/sell 120 round trip gives gross gain 20 cents. With half-spread 1, adverse slip 1 and fee 1, buy fill 112 costs 113 including fee, so cash after buy=1000-2*113=774.
Sell fill 118 nets 117 including fee; cash ends 774+2*117=1008. Difference from gross 1020 is 12=2 shares*2 sides*(1 spread+1 slip+1 fee). Marked equity at the intermediate 115 close is 1004.

This fixed quantity/path comparison isolates drag. Costs can change affordability, which changes fills and future positions. Across different trade paths, you cannot subtract a universal cost number from an unchanged gross return and call it the simulated net strategy.

blocks.caption: Expected: gross 1020 net 1008 drag 12; fills/cash ((0,None,1000),(2,112,774),(-2,118,1008)); partial 1 expired 1 final 1004; no fill final 1000; costs exceed supported sell proceeds. Full repeated engine so no fragment import needed. Capacity 1 allows only one opening buy; remainder expires. Zero capacity produces no fee/fill. These capacities are supplied opening scenarios, not future full-bar volume used at the open.

blocks.md: An opening target delta is capped by supplied executable capacity, affordable buy size including fees, and current sell holdings. A full-day volume participation cap would only be known after that day unless modeled as an ex-post allocation rule with declared timing; do not feed it into a point-in-time open decision unnoticed. Capacity scenarios are not queue position or fill-probability models. In a losing strategy, less execution may improve realized returns; do not promise every more conservative assumption makes every backtest PnL monotonically lower.

An OHLC bar can show that a price level was reached without showing whether your order was already present, its queue priority, available size or the path between extremes. If both a stop and target lie within the range, their order cannot generally be inferred from OHLC alone. Use finer data or explicit conservative/alternative path scenarios, record ambiguity and retain no-fill alternatives. This capstone does not implement stop/limit/OHLC touch fills; do not infer they were validated.

QuantConnect documents complete fills for pre-built backtest models and default zero slippage under its default brokerage model. Its EquityFillModel has source-specific data/order rules, such as strict low<buy-limit/high>sell-limit for documented limit cases; these differ from inclusive touch models. Backtrader documents next-bar execution and configurable slip behavior. Defaults are not evidence of real liquidity or your broker's costs. Keep chosen library/config/version/data granularity and any custom overrides in the experiment manifest.

Compare no-cost/finite-cost, low/high spread, capacity 0/1/full, delays, missing/stale data and different liquidation policies. Include turnover, filled/unfilled quantity, fees, exposure and terminal inventory, not only net Sharpe. Compare baselines under the SAME data/timing/cost rules. Historical SEC investor education explains that execution takes time, quoted size is finite and actual price can differ; its 2013 page is used for these basic concepts, not current regulatory requirements or modern broker routing details.

Independent transfer: choose enough cash so fixed-path quantities do not change, and algebraically reconcile round-trip drag across several cost settings. Then deliberately cross affordability thresholds and show why the path changes. Set capacity 0 and prove fees zero, change only a future capacity and verify unchanged earlier prefix. Sketch two intrabar paths with identical OHLC but different stop/target order and state why neither is uniquely identified by the bar. No live order is sent.

Sources: [Backtrader slippage limits/configuration](https://www.backtrader.com/docu/slippage/slippage/), [QuantConnect fill concepts](https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/trade-fills/key-concepts), [slippage concepts/defaults](https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/slippage/key-concepts), [equity-specific fill rules](https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/trade-fills/supported-models/equity-model), [SEC 2013 basic execution education](https://www.sec.gov/investor/pubs/tradexec.htm). Our symmetric cents stress and capacity interface are own design.

guidedExercise.prompt: Why can a zero-fee OHLC backtest still be too optimistic even if its cash arithmetic is perfect?
guidedExercise.solution: Fill price/size/timing may assume unavailable liquidity or same-bar knowledge; OHLC does not establish queue/path, spread/slippage/impact/delay and terminal liquidation can matter. Need documented data/model/defaults, cost references and sensitivity/no-fill cases. Arithmetic consistency is not realistic execution or future performance.

independentExercise.prompt: Write a small test case that deliberately breaks the contract boundary in "Costs, slippage and fill assumptions" and verify how your implementation rejects or handles it.
hints: Test zero, negative, empty, duplicate, and boundary values.
Confirm both time/memory complexity and numerical precision remain within spec.

commonMistakes: A cost field needs its reference and units. (Add only costs not already represented.)
Touch is weaker evidence than an actual fill record. (Order timing/queue/size remain unknown.)
realWorldApplication: In practice, engineering teams apply costs, slippage and fill assumptions within Research Infrastructure and Backtesting when building reliable backtesting and quant modelling workflows — specifically to apply separate adverse half-spread, slippage and per-unit fee assumptions to signed fills and reconcile a fixed-path gross/net round trip.
quantFinanceApplication: Desk workflows in Research Infrastructure and Backtesting rely on costs, slippage and fill assumptions across backtesting, quant modelling, data infrastructure, keeping numerical estimates, risk bounds, and low-latency paths predictable.
summary: State execution references and separate spread/slippage/fees without double counting.
Capacity and affordability change trade paths; OHLC touch does not prove queued executable volume.
Stress scenarios and honest defaults are evidence of modeled assumptions, not live fill or future net-return guarantees.

quiz.prompt: A buy fills at an already observed ask. What avoids spread double counting?
options: Always add the full spread again
Treat all fees as price returns
quiz.explanation: A cost field needs its reference and units. (Add only costs not already represented.)

quiz.prompt: A bar low touches a buy limit. What does OHLC alone establish?
options: A level was reached, not your fill
The level could be filled at unlimited size without changing the historical path
quiz.explanation: Touch is weaker evidence than an actual fill record. (Order timing/queue/size remain unknown.)

quiz.prompt: Worked 2-share round trip: 1 spread+1 slip+1 fee cents per side. Total drag cents?
quiz.explanation: Applying the rule from Costs, slippage and fill assumptions, 2 shares*2 sides*3 cents=12 — double-check units, sign conventions, and boundaries.

quiz.prompt: Why not use full-day volume as known at that day's open?
options: The final volume is future information then
Volume always has no trading relevance
It is the same as an opening executable quote size
quiz.explanation: Capacity clocks must match the modeled execution time. (A declared ex-post model is a different timing assumption.)

quiz.prompt: Higher modeled costs reduce affordable buy size. Which comparison is valid?
options: Subtract old fixed drag despite changed quantities
Treat the original gross path as unchanged truth
Claim PnL must fall on every possible strategy
quiz.explanation: Preserve affordability and execution feedback. (Separate fixed-path drag from path feedback.)
